page_title: File Architect - Create File and Folder Structures From Plain Text

summary.name: File Architect
summary.one_liner: File Architect is an app that creates file and folder structures on disk from a plain-text, tab-indented outline.
use_cases: Setting up a new software project folder layout
Creating template folder structures for recurring work
Generating many empty or blank files at once
Organizing project files with an AI-described structure
Copying or renaming existing files into a new structure
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you write files and folders as an indented text outline, using tabs for nesting, and creates them on your machine. Lines with a file extension create files; if a blank template file for that type is available it is used, so files open in their apps right away. It supports saving structures and replacements for reuse, plus templates. An AI creation feature builds a structure from a plain-English description. It can also copy, move, and rename existing files or folders into the new structure. The page says it supports 60+ file types.
notable: Blank files open directly in their applications, unlike zero-byte empty files
Source code is open on GitHub (app and engine/core repositories)
AI creation turns a text description into a structure using Google Gemini
Stores templates and structures locally on the user's machine
caveats: Free 7-day trial; continued use appears to require a license, and commercial use (business of more than 2 persons) is a paid case per the FAQ
AI creation sends prompts to Google Gemini
Platform list on the page names only the app; the listing context suggests macOS
